# Abstract

<!--# Ca. 150 words -->

Stratigraphic paleobiology seeks to understand how physical processes shape the fossil record, whereas phylogenetics seeks to reconstruct evolutionary relationships, rates, and times. Although stratigraphy is the key source of time in phylogenies and reconstructed evolutionary trees allow us to fill gaps in the fossil record, few studies apply both approaches simultaneously. The challenge of reconciling physical geological record with phylogenetics lies in theoretical chasms between disciplines, computational tools available to researchers, and ontologies of uncertainty. Meanwhile recent advances in modelling in both areas create opportunities for joint models of stratigraphic and phylogenetic processes. In this workshop, we will isolate these opportunities and invite stratigraphers, evolutionary biologists and software engineers to solve them together interactively. This workshops aims to establish a theoretical framework for incorporating geological record in phylogenetic inference and to translate these theoretical advances into actionable research software improvements.
